Everything is pushed to GitHub, and the current compaction setup is tagged `compaction-baseline` so you can compare later versions against it.

- **Commit:** `docs/engine-book/` (66 files, including the two PDFs) went to `main` as `2ec6812`. I found nothing that looked like a secret before committing. There was nothing else uncommitted, so the code is unchanged.
- **Tag:** `compaction-baseline` points at that commit. It records the current setup: 80% trigger, the pruner that keeps the first 4k and last 1k characters, and saving outputs over 50 KB to a file.

Local `main` and GitHub now match. To see what changed later, run `git diff compaction-baseline..HEAD -- packages/compaction packages/spill`, or open `https://github.com/poojarishreyas/Elemental_harness/compare/compaction-baseline...main`.

For the compaction work, I'd do each phase on its own branch and tag it when done (`compaction-phase1`, and so on), so you can diff any two versions. Should I start Phase 1 (the pruner changes) on a new branch?
